predecessors.name: Judea
predecessors.text: Iturea, Trachonitis, Batanea, Gaulanitis, Auranitis and Paneas, the northern part of Herod the Great's kingdom

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Philip's territories, briefly added to the Province of Syria after his death in 34

successors.name: Kingdom of Herod Agrippa I
successors.text: 'In 37 CE, Philip's former territories were given to Agrippa I, who was made king'

ledger.x: 4 BCE: Philip becomes tetrarch of the north.
4 BCE: the tetrarchy is a Roman client from Augustus's confirmation of Herod's will ('Augustus largely confirmed the division of territory set out by Herod in his final will').
34: Philip dies and Rome takes the tetrarchy.
34: the tetrarchy is added to the province of Syria.
34: Philip dies and the tetrarchy ends.

certainty.note: No page gives the tetrarchy's boundaries; Golan and Hauran stand for the six districts.
